en.name: Soup base, beef or vegetable
en.summary: Soup base is the concentrated paste form of stock — saltier and wetter than a stock cube. There is no fixed unopened figure: follow the use-by date on the package. Once opened, refrigerate it, which is the instruction printed on most jars and the one that matters.
en.pantry: An unopened jar or tub keeps in a cool, dark cupboard to the use-by date printed on the package, and this page will not put a number alongside that date, because none is published. What holds an unopened base stable is its salt concentration and the seal — not any sterilisation you can rely on after opening. Keep it away from the hob, since heat drives off the aromatics and darkens the paste, and never store an opened jar in the cupboard however salty the paste is.
en.fridge: Refrigerate after opening: that is the instruction on the package and it is not optional. Once the seal is broken you have a moist, low-acid, protein-rich paste that has been exposed to air and to whatever spoon went into it, so keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below with the lid on tight. Use a clean dry spoon every time, wipe the rim before closing it, and go by the manufacturer's guidance on the jar for how long to keep it after opening — different products vary a great deal.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for soup base. It can be frozen and will be safe indefinitely at −18 °C (0 °F), and the high salt means it will not freeze completely solid, which makes it easy to scoop — but no published figure exists, so this page will not supply one. If you use a base slowly, freezing teaspoon-sized portions in an ice cube tray and bagging them is a practical way to avoid a jar sitting half-used in the fridge for months.
en.thawing: There is no need to thaw it — spoon out what you need and stir it straight into hot liquid.
spoilage: Mould at the surface or around the rim of the jar.
A sour or fermented smell rather than a roasted, savoury one.
Paste that has gone runny, bubbly or lifted from the sides of the jar.
A colour change to grey or a dull, dark crust that was not there before.
tips: Write the opening date on the lid.
Use a clean dry spoon and wipe the rim before resealing.
Freeze portions in an ice cube tray if a jar lasts you months.
Taste before salting the dish; base is much saltier than home-made stock.

faq.q: How long does soup base keep?
faq.a: Unopened, follow the use-by date on the package — no general figure is published. After opening, refrigerate it and follow the maker's guidance.

faq.q: Does soup base need to be refrigerated after opening?
faq.a: Yes. The label says so, and once the seal is broken the paste is a moist, low-acid food regardless of how salty it tastes.
No timeline is published, but it freezes without trouble and the salt keeps it scoopable. An ice cube tray works well.

zh.name: 濃縮高湯醬
zh.summary: 高湯醬是濃縮成膏狀的高湯——比高湯塊更鹹也更濕。未開封沒有固定天數：請以包裝上的有效日期為準。開封後要冷藏，那是多數罐子上印著的指示，也是真正重要的那一條。
zh.pantry: 未開封的罐裝或盒裝放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃，到包裝印的有效日期為止；本頁不會在那個日期旁邊再加一個數字，因為沒有公布值。讓未開封的高湯醬穩定的是它的鹽度和封口——而不是某種你開封後還能依賴的滅菌。請遠離爐台，高溫會把香氣趕走、也會讓醬色變深；而且不管醬多鹹，開封後的罐子都不要放回櫥櫃。
zh.fridge: 開封後冷藏：這是包裝上的指示，不是選項。封口一破，你手上就是一份含水、低酸、蛋白質豐富的醬，而且已經接觸過空氣和伸進去的湯匙，所以請蓋緊放 4 °C 以下。每次用乾淨乾燥的湯匙、蓋回去之前把罐口擦乾淨，開封後能放多久請依罐上廠商的說明——不同產品差異很大。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給高湯醬的冷凍期限。它可以冷凍，在 −18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，而且高鹽讓它不會完全凍成硬塊、很好挖——但沒有公布的數字，所以本頁不提供。如果你用得很慢，用製冰盒凍成一小匙一小匙再裝袋，是避免一罐在冰箱裡半開著放好幾個月的實用做法。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍——挖出需要的量，直接拌進熱湯裡即可。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有發酵味，而不是烘烤過的鹹香。
醬體變稀、起泡，或從罐壁浮起來。
顏色轉灰，或出現原本沒有的暗沉硬殼。
tips: 用乾淨乾燥的湯匙，蓋回去之前先擦罐口。
一罐要用好幾個月的話，先用製冰盒分份冷凍。
調味前先試味道；高湯醬比自製高湯鹹得多。

faq.a: 未開封請以包裝上的有效日期為準，沒有通用數字。開封後冷藏，並依廠商說明。

faq.q: 高湯醬開封後要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 要。標示上就這麼寫，而且封口一破，不管它嘗起來多鹹，它都是含水、低酸的食品。
沒有公布的期限，但它很好凍，而且鹽分讓它仍然挖得動。用製冰盒分份效果很好。
